response.sql:
WITH scan_ratio AS (
  SELECT s.arcref, p.fundflux, s.gbsize / NULLIF(s.spanmin, 0) AS ratio
  FROM scans s
  JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref
),
group_rate AS (
  SELECT arcref, fundflux, AVG(ratio) AS rate
  FROM scan_ratio
  WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY arcref, fundflux
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS bench FROM group_rate
)
SELECT g.arcref AS project_ref, g.fundflux AS funding_source, g.rate AS rate, g.rate - b.bench AS excess
FROM group_rate g
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE g.rate > b.bench
ORDER BY excess DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Scans are matched to projects with an inner join on scans.arcref = projects.arcregistry, so scans with no matching project are dropped.
A scan's ratio is missing when gbsize or spanmin is NULL, or when spanmin is 0 (NULLIF turns zero duration into NULL, avoiding division by zero). Those scans are ignored.
Rows with a NULL funding source (fundflux) form their own group, since SQL groups NULLs together. The request does not say whether they should be kept or dropped.
The benchmark is the unweighted mean of group rates, over only the groups that have at least one computable ratio. Groups with no computable ratio have no rate and are excluded.

alternatives.interpretation: Drop scans whose project has no funding source (fundflux IS NULL) before grouping, so every group has a named funding source.

WITH scan_ratio AS (
  SELECT s.arcref, p.fundflux, s.gbsize / NULLIF(s.spanmin, 0) AS ratio
  FROM scans s
  JOIN projects p ON p.arcregistry = s.arcref
  WHERE p.fundflux IS NOT NULL
),
group_rate AS (
  SELECT arcref, fundflux, AVG(ratio) AS rate
  FROM scan_ratio
  WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY arcref, fundflux
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS bench FROM group_rate
)
SELECT g.arcref AS project_ref, g.fundflux AS funding_source, g.rate AS rate, g.rate - b.bench AS excess
FROM group_rate g
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE g.rate > b.bench
ORDER BY excess DESC
LIMIT 10;
